A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same signed-graph defense for multi-agent systems. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable, and retained material can be matched across renaming, restructuring, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 experiments measuring task performance and malicious-agent detection, including attack comparisons, dynamic graphs, and a backpropagation ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds adaptive and combined attacks, threshold sensitivity, runtime measurements, scalability experiments, and human validation of edge scoring.

M1.justification: The temporal DAG, ternary edge scoring, backward score averaging, agent-level deviation threshold, and outgoing-message pruning remain the same. Naming the method BPD, adding Algorithm 1, and expanding its mathematical description do not establish a different algorithm.

E1.justification: MMLU, Alpaca, SAMSum, and ChatDoctor remain unchanged. However, Sections 4.6–4.8 substantially extend the adversarial scenarios to corrupted scoring, attackers informed about topology and detector scores, and combined Harmful+Reframing and Suboptimal+Reframing attacks. These alter the evaluated threat conditions beyond v1's individual attacks and dynamic graphs.

E2.justification: G-Safeguard, AGENTXPOSED, Challenger, and Inspector retain their membership in corresponding comparisons. This includes the DeepSeek-V3 text-generation comparison, moved from v1 Table 13 to v2 Table 18. The new experiments introduce no new external defense baseline.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include score-sign manipulation, disclosure of system information to attackers, a threshold sweep from 1.3 to 1.7, runtime measurements, and scaling to 7/10 agents and five dialogue rounds. Appendix B.4 adds exact-match evaluation against human labels on 50 sampled items. The original benchmark settings remain; Appendix A.1 primarily clarifies their implementation.

E4.justification: The original backpropagation ablation is retained. v2 adds substantial analyses of threshold sensitivity, robustness to compromised scoring and informed or combined attacks, computational overhead and scaling, and agreement between human and LLM edge scores (Sections 4.5–4.9 and Appendices B.3–B.4).

E5.justification: Table 1 newly states that three experiments were conducted, and Tables 1–2 report means with one standard deviation instead of point estimates alone. This reporting remains confined to the main GPT-4o/MMLU comparisons. v1 provides no run count, so an increase in runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 contain revised values: BPD's reported average answer accuracy changes from 86%/87% to 85.4%/87.5%, now with uncertainty. New system-aware attack results report 83%/85% answer accuracy and 81%/82% detection accuracy, alongside new threshold, combined-attack, timing, and scorer-alignment results. Other original tables retain their values after equivalent rescaling and renumbering.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 adds a finite layerwise matrix-product expression for propagated scores and explicitly states uniqueness through a single backward pass on the DAG. It also specifies zero-outdegree handling and formalizes the PageRank comparison. Most remaining mathematics reformulates the existing recursion; no substantial theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution and superior-defense claims remain. v2 replaces v1's continuous-monitoring and edge-restoration language with explicit per-query detection and pruning, emphasizes training-free operation, and adds a quantified low-runtime-overhead claim to the introduction.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation: threshold choice trades removal of useful communication against missed attacks; combined-attack resilience is attributed to decomposed local judgments; and low overhead is attributed to inexpensive sentence-pair scoring. It also discusses incompatible attack combinations and introduces a Byzantine-threshold scope limitation. The existing explanation involving isolation of infected benign agents is retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 specifies synchronous three-round schedules, 15/12 temporal nodes, 20/10 review messages, and detailed feedback routing. v2 also supplies runtime information and updates the stated code location to the BPD repository, while removing the separate future-release reproducibility statement. Existing prompts and baseline configurations are retained; these are principally documentation refinements.

R1.justification: v2 adds the BLEURT reference by Sellam et al. and removes background references including Brown et al., Kushwaha et al., and Yu et al. Related work is reorganized into attack and defense categories while retaining the main local-versus-global positioning. Numerous other bibliography changes concern publication metadata rather than different works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition are substantially rewritten. BPD becomes the consistent method name, the methodology gains named stages and a summary, and the experimental narrative is reorganized into more focused subsections. Appendix organization and closing statements also change.

P2.justification: The main text switches to a two-column layout, Figure 1 is extensively redrawn, and tables are rebuilt with separate structure/method grouping and percentage displays. v2 adds Algorithm 1, two threshold figures, and seven result tables. Retained appendix tables are renumbered, and the misleading caption of v1 Table 14 is corrected in v2 Table 19.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of previously untested weaknesses: scorer corruption, informed and combined adversaries, scorer reliability, and computational cost. Uncertainty reporting and explicit MAS schedules also improve transparency. These address important evidential gaps in v1. Reporting remains imperfect: uncertainty covers only two tables, and the introduction's below-10% overhead claim conflicts with the 10.6% hierarchy overhead in Section 4.9. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial added validation.
